title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
question: What growth and cash-flow assumptions does $263.75 still price in after the November 20 selloff, and how does TXN stack up against analog peers?

epigraph.quote: A lower stock price does not automatically create a margin of safety if enterprise value still embeds double-digit free-cash-flow compounding ahead of a major cash acquisition.
epigraph.author: Institutional Underwriting Desk

web_blocks.html: At $263.75 per share on November 20, 2026, Texas Instruments carries a $241.01B market cap on 914.00M shares (921M diluted in Q3 2026).[12][27] On pre-November-9 Finviz debt figures, enterprise value sits at $246.42B. Including the November 9 $2.0B senior notes issue—which lifted pro-forma cash to $10,129M and debt principal to $15,650M ($5,521M net debt)—pro-forma EV is $246.53B.[28][29] Trailing multiples remain full despite the week's -13.13% drop: 34.22x TTM P/E ($7.71 EPS), 32.93x Finviz P/FCF (or 35.18x on $6.85B ex-CHIPS TTM FCF), 22.81x EV/EBITDA, and 11.87x EV/Sales ($20.77B TTM sales).[12][27] On consensus forward estimates (~$11.65 EPS), TXN trades at 22.64x Forward P/E with a 2.19% trailing dividend yield ($5.78 TTM; 2.31% on the $6.08 annualized rate).[9][12]

Our Reverse DCF at $246.53B pro-forma EV shows why $263.75 is still no bargain. Our base schedule uses an 8.5% WACC and a 3.5% terminal growth rate.[12][15] That 8.5% hurdle reflects historical mega-cap analog multiple compression and sits roughly 200 bps below strict CAPM (9.5%–10.5% WACC at a 5.04% US10Y yield, 1.38–1.68 beta, ~4.0% equity risk premium, and ~6% debt weight).[12][15] Starting from $6.85B in normalized ex-CHIPS TTM FCF and deducting the $7.5B Silicon Labs cash outlay in Year 1, $263.75 embeds a 10.0% 10-year core FCF CAGR.[6][27][32] Our bridge uses analyst/model underwriting assumptions—not filed Silicon Labs disclosures—that Silicon Labs scales to $0.65B in Year-3 FCF including $450M in targeted synergies.[6][32]

At that 10.0% CAGR, combined Year-10 unlevered FCF must reach $19.03B (~47%–48% FCF margin on ~$40B combined 2036 revenue). Reconciling that ~$40B Year-10 figure with Chapter 5's $24B–$28B+ standalone capacity requires three bridges. First, Silicon Labs contributes ~$1.0B of baseline wireless revenue compounding over a decade. Second, wafer price and mix shift higher across Sherman, Richardson, and Lehi toward 48V AI data-center power, auto, and industrial chips. Third, scaling from $24B–$28B+ to ~$40B assumes additional post-2030 equipment spend inside the pre-built SM2 and LFAB2 cleanroom shells beyond the near-term $2B–$3B Phase 1/2 shell capex band.[1][4][6]

web_blocks.the_number: $295.00 per share Base Case 12-month fair value (+11.8% above $263.75 CMP) at an 8.5% hurdle, dropping to $198.28 Base at a strict 10.5% CAPM WACC.
web_blocks.how_calculated: We blend two institutional methods: a 10-year unlevered DCF (8.5% base WACC, 3.5% terminal growth, explicit -$7.5B Silicon Labs outflow in Year 1, stress-tested across 9.5%–10.5% CAPM WACC) and a 25.3x forward earnings multiple on ~$11.65 consensus FY2027E EPS.
web_blocks.the_inputs: Normalized ex-CHIPS TTM FCF of $6.85B; pro-forma net debt of $5.52B ($15.65B debt less $10.13B cash); 914.0M share count; 35% OBBBA Section 48D ITC offset; $2.14B remaining CHIPS receivables; and analyst/model underwriting assumptions of $0.65B Year-3 SLAB FCF and $450M targeted synergies (not filed SLAB disclosures).
web_blocks.the_range: At 8.5% WACC, flexing 10-year core FCF growth from 8.0% to 13.5% produces $220.00 to $350.00. Under strict CAPM WACC of 9.5%–10.5% (5.04% US10Y, 1.38 beta), Base DCF drops from $295.00 to $238.25 (9.5% WACC) and $198.28 (10.5% WACC). Combined bear stress (10.0% WACC, 8.0% standalone FCF CAGR, and a $519M Year-1 regulatory failure hit from the $499M SLAB break fee plus $20M 101% SMR premium) yields $160.62.
web_blocks.if_off: Our $295.00 Base estimate drops below $200 ($198.28) if 10.5% CAPM discount rates prevail, or to $160.62 if the 12% single Analog buyer cuts orders, China tariffs hit ~50% physical shipments, or regulators trigger the $499M SLAB break fee and $20M SMR premium.

web_blocks.takeaway: At 8.5% WACC (~200 bps below strict CAPM), $263.75 embeds 10.0% FCF compounding. At CAPM-aligned 9.5%–10.5% WACC, Base DCF falls to $238.25–$198.28, while combined bear stress (10.0% WACC, 8.0% standalone FCF CAGR, and the $519M SLAB break fee plus 101% SMR hit*) drops to $160.62. The $225.00–$240.00 band is therefore a conditional watch zone only at an 8.5%–9.5% hurdle—not a hard floor if 10.5% CAPM rates persist.

web_blocks.html: Why Pre-Funding, OBBBA Tax Credits & China Risk Alter the Bridge: Pass 1 uncovered four cash and balance-sheet drivers that sharpen our valuation discipline. First, the November 9 $2.0B senior notes (5.000%–5.750% coupons) carry a 101% Special Mandatory Redemption clause if Silicon Labs fails to close, while the Merger Agreement exposes TXN to a $499M reverse termination fee.[28][33] Second, Silicon Labs generated 30.9% of 9M 2026 sales in China and 20.0% in Taiwan, compounding TXN's own 23% China-HQ and ~50% physical ship-into-China exposure.[27][31][32] Third, the July 2025 OBBBA lifted TXN's Section 48D ITC from 25% to 35% alongside $2,136M in CHIPS receivables, cushioning 2026–2028 capex.[27] Fourth, one unnamed Analog buyer accounts for 12% of total revenue (~$2.12B in FY2025), creating single-socket volatility if personal electronics orders soften.[31]

10-Year Valuation Bands vs. 5.04% Treasury Yields: Over 2016–2025, TXN traded at 18x–28x forward earnings during mid-cycle expansions, while dividend yields above 2.8%–3.2% marked true cyclical bargains.[7][12] At 2.19% trailing yield (2.31% annualized at $6.08/sh) and 11.87x EV/Sales, TXN still sits above pre-2020 valuation floors (7x–9x EV/Sales). Meanwhile, risk-free rates stay elevated: the US 10-year Treasury yields 5.04% and the 2-year yields 4.76%.[15] Earning a +6.07% probability-weighted expected equity return inside a broken downtrend does not compensate investors for equity beta when T-bills yield nearly 4.8%.

web_blocks.html: The updated peer table strips away any illusion of deep relative cheapness. ADI ($345.92) fell -15.35% on the week and now trades at 20.53x Forward P/E—two turns cheaper than TXN's 22.64x despite growing quarterly sales +39.63% YoY versus TXN's +27.69%.[12][18] Meanwhile, Tier-2 names NXPI (12.82x Fwd P/E, 17.04x P/FCF, 14.63% ROIC), MCHP (12.57x Fwd P/E, 3.28% yield), and ON (12.83x Fwd P/E, 12.00x EV/EBITDA) trade at 40%–45% forward discounts to TXN.[19][20][21] TXN deserves a Tier-1 quality premium for its 22.04% ROIC and 300mm cost edge, yet paying 22.64x forward earnings and 35.18x ex-CHIPS FCF while the entire analog group breaks down offers zero margin of safety.

Valuation Trigger: Maintain primary new-capital verdict at REJECTED (TIER_0) and EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 6.7226 held shares. Treat $225.00–$240.00 (~19.3x–20.6x Forward P/E) strictly as a conditional Stage 1 watch zone valid only at an 8.5%–9.5% discount rate; at a 10.5% CAPM WACC, Base DCF drops below $200 ($198.28, or $160.62 under combined bear stress with the $519M SLAB break/SMR hit), requiring sub-$200 pricing or ex-CHIPS FCF above $9.0B/yr with >60% gross margin if Treasury yields stay above 5%.

book_paragraphs: At $263.75 per share on November 20, 2026, Texas Instruments commands a $241.01 billion market capitalization on 914.00 million shares. Incorporating the November 9, 2026 $2.0 billion senior notes closing—which lifted pro-forma cash and short-term investments to $10,129 million against $15,650 million of total debt principal—pro-forma enterprise value stands at $246.53 billion ($246.42 billion on pre-offering Finviz figures). After sliding 13.13% this week in the facts ledger (-15.41% on TradingView), TXN now trades at 34.22 times trailing earnings ($7.71 EPS), 32.93 times Finviz free cash flow (or 35.18 times $6.85 billion ex-CHIPS TTM FCF), 22.81 times EV/EBITDA, and 11.87 times EV/Sales.

On forward consensus expectations (~$11.65 EPS), the multiple reads 22.64 times Forward P/E alongside a 2.19% trailing dividend yield ($5.78 TTM, or 2.31% forward at the $6.08 annualized rate). At first glance, a 22.64x forward multiple for a 22.04% ROIC franchise looks tempting. Yet a rigorous Reverse DCF proves that $263.75 still embeds aggressive multi-year assumptions—especially once we account for the pending $7.5 billion cash outlay for Silicon Labs.

Our base model uses an 8.5% weighted average cost of capital and a 3.5% terminal growth rate. That 8.5% hurdle sits roughly 200 basis points below strict CAPM (9.5%–10.5% WACC given a 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield, 1.38–1.68 beta, and ~4% equity risk premium). Starting from $6.85 billion in normalized ex-CHIPS FCF and deducting the $7.5 billion Silicon Labs outlay in Year 1, our bridge uses analyst/model underwriting assumptions—not filed Silicon Labs disclosures—that Silicon Labs scales to $0.65 billion of Year-3 FCF including $450 million of targeted 300mm synergies. At $246.53 billion enterprise value, $263.75 still prices in a 10.0% ten-year core FCF CAGR, reaching $19.03 billion in combined Year-10 FCF on ~$40 billion of 2036 revenue. Reconciling that ~$40 billion Year-10 level with Chapter 5's $24 billion to $28 billion+ standalone capacity reflects acquired Silicon Labs revenue, price/mix gains across Sherman, Richardson, and Lehi wafers, and additional post-2030 equipment spending in SM2 and LFAB2 shells beyond the near-term $2 billion to $3 billion Phase 1/2 shell capex.

At an 8.5% hurdle, our Base Case 12-month fair value stands at $295.00 per share (+11.8% above CMP), with a $350.00 Bull Case and $220.00 Bear Case. However, testing strict 9.5%–10.5% CAPM discount rates strips away any illusion of cheapness: Base DCF drops to $238.25 at 9.5% WACC and $198.28 at 10.5% WACC. Under combined bear stress—10.0% WACC, 8.0% standalone FCF compounding without Silicon Labs, and a $519 million Year-1 regulatory failure hit ($499 million reverse break fee plus $20 million 101% SMR premium on the November 9 notes)—intrinsic value falls to $160.62.

book_subsections.title: Historical Valuation Bands, 5.04% Rates & The 5-Peer Analog Matrix
paragraphs: Historical valuation bands reinforce the need for patience. Between 2016 and 2025, TXN consistently found major cyclical bottoms only when its dividend yield exceeded 2.8% to 3.2% and EV/Sales compressed toward 7x to 9x. Today's 2.19% trailing yield and 11.87x EV/Sales remain comfortably above those historical trough zones, even as risk-free 2-year and 10-year U.S. Treasuries yield 4.76% and 5.04%. In a 5% rate regime, investors should demand a wide margin of safety before stepping into cyclical semiconductors.

To be sure, TXN continues to benefit from generous U.S. manufacturing support. Under the July 2025 OBBBA legislation, TXN's qualifying Section 48D Investment Tax Credit stepped up from 25% to 35% for assets placed in service after 2025, backed by $2,136 million in balance-sheet CHIPS receivables on top of $630 million already collected. That subsidy reduces net capital intensity over 2026–2028, supporting our $295.00 Base Case.

Yet comparing TXN against its four live-tracked analog peers—ADI, NXPI, MCHP, and ON (note STM is absent from the November 20 snapshot)—confirms that relative valuation offers no urgent buy signal either. All five stocks fell sharply this week into Stage 4 downtrends. Analog Devices ($345.92) now trades at 20.53x Forward P/E, cheaper than TXN's 22.64x despite delivering +39.63% quarterly revenue growth versus TXN's +27.69%. Meanwhile, NXPI ($235.15) trades at 12.82x Forward P/E and 17.04x P/FCF with 14.63% ROIC, while MCHP ($55.44) and ON ($60.84) trade below 13x forward earnings.

Put the DCF math, CAPM sensitivity, historical yield bands, and peer multiples together: TXN remains a premier 22.04% ROIC compounder, yet at $263.75 it offers neither deep value nor clean relative cheapness. Even the $225.00 to $240.00 band (~19.3x–20.6x Forward P/E, ~9.0% implied FCF CAGR) is strictly a conditional watch zone under an 8.5%–9.5% WACC—once we apply a full 10.5% CAPM WACC, Base DCF drops below $200 to $198.28 ($160.62 under combined bear stress). That reinforces our primary REJECTED (TIER_0) verdict on new capital and EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on held shares.
